slots.practicalActivity: In your Oracle Fusion practice environment, open the Subledger Accounting work area and locate the accounting events generated by a transaction you already created in an earlier course (an AP invoice or AR receipt), identifying its event class and event type. Then diagram where SLA sits between that subledger and the General Ledger.
slots.deliverable: A diagram of SLA's position between subledger and GL, plus the event class/type you identified on a real transaction.

slots.practicalActivity: Open Manage Accounting Methods and inspect the seeded standard accrual method assigned to your ledger. Then, for at least 3 subledger applications (Payables, Receivables, Fixed Assets), list the type of source document each hands to SLA (invoice, receipt, asset addition).
slots.deliverable: Notes on the accounting method you inspected, plus a 3-row table of subledger application -> source document type.

lessons.title: Journal Line Types and Journal Line Rules

slots.practicalActivity: Open an existing journal line rule for a Payables event (such as Invoice Validated) and identify its journal line type, side (debit/credit), and condition. Then open the account rule attached to one of its segments and identify whether it derives from a constant, a source value, or a mapping set.
slots.deliverable: Written notes identifying one real journal line rule's type/side/condition and one real account rule's derivation method.

slots.practicalActivity: Build your own mapping set that translates at least 4 input values (such as expense categories) into 4 output GL segment values. Then build a description rule that concatenates at least two source values (such as supplier name and invoice number) into a readable journal line description.
slots.deliverable: One created mapping set (4+ input/output pairs) and one created description rule, both saved in your practice environment.

slots.practicalActivity: Add a supporting reference to an existing journal line rule (for example, tagging the AP invoice number onto the accrual line) and confirm, on a sample transaction, that the reference value actually appears on the generated journal line.
slots.deliverable: One supporting reference attached to a journal line rule, verified present on a sample journal entry.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter lab: without referring back to the lessons, build one complete rule chain from scratch -- a journal line rule, an account rule using a mapping set you create, a description rule, and one supporting reference -- then trace through on paper what journal line it would produce for a sample transaction.
slots.deliverable: One self-built rule chain (journal line rule + account rule + mapping set + description rule + supporting reference) with a hand-traced sample journal line.

slots.practicalActivity: Open the seeded Application Accounting Definition for Payables and review its journal entry rule set assignments. Then copy it and modify one journal line rule in your copy (without touching the seeded original) to reflect a different account derivation.
slots.deliverable: One copied Application Accounting Definition with one modified journal line rule, with the original seeded definition left untouched.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a new Subledger Accounting Method that references your modified Application Accounting Definition from Slot 7. Then assign that method to a test ledger (or review what reassigning an existing ledger's method would require).
slots.deliverable: One new Subledger Accounting Method referencing your custom definition, assigned to (or mapped against) a ledger.

slots.practicalActivity: Run validation on your Application Accounting Definition and Subledger Accounting Method from Slots 7-8, resolve any validation error it reports, and activate the definition once it passes.
slots.deliverable: A validated and activated Application Accounting Definition, with any validation errors you hit and fixed noted.

lessons.title: Creating Accounting in Payables and Receivables

slots.practicalActivity: Run Create Accounting in Draft mode for a real AP invoice and a real AR transaction, review both draft journal entries, then rerun Create Accounting in Final mode for one of them and confirm its status changes from Draft to Final.
slots.deliverable: One draft and one final subledger journal entry, created from a real Payables or Receivables transaction.

slots.practicalActivity: Use Review Journal Entries to inspect your Slot 10 final entry's header and lines in detail. Then deliberately introduce an error (an incomplete account rule) on a new transaction, run Create Accounting, and correct the resulting error following the lesson's correction steps.
slots.deliverable: A detailed review of one final journal entry, plus a log of one deliberately caused accounting error and how you corrected it.

slots.practicalActivity: Transfer your Slot 10 final journal entry to the General Ledger, then run Journal Import and confirm the GL journal that lands references back to the originating subledger entry.
slots.deliverable: One GL journal created from your subledger entry via transfer and journal import, with the back-reference to the subledger entry confirmed.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter lab: run a second transaction, from a different subledger application than Slots 10-12, all the way from Create Accounting (draft, then final) through transfer and journal import to a posted GL journal, without referring back to the lessons.
slots.deliverable: A second, independently run transaction carried from draft accounting through to a posted GL journal.

lessons.title: Subledger Reports: Journal Entries and Account Analysis

slots.practicalActivity: Run the Journal Entries and Account Analysis reports for your test ledger covering the transactions you created this chapter. Then run an Open Account Balances Listing for the accrual or suspense account they touched.
slots.deliverable: Two generated reports (a journal/account-analysis report and an open account balances listing) covering your own test transactions.

slots.practicalActivity: Reconcile your subledger's trial balance against the corresponding GL account for the transactions you've created across this course. Then review the accounting attribute assignments on one subledger application to confirm which attributes (like accounted amount) feed SLA.
slots.deliverable: A reconciliation memo tying your subledger activity to GL, plus notes on one application's accounting attribute assignments.

slots.practicalActivity: Deliberately break one checkpoint in a new transaction (an inactive account rule, a mapping set missing an output value) and troubleshoot it back to its root cause using Review Journal Entries and the error logs, documenting each diagnostic step.
slots.deliverable: A troubleshooting log for one deliberately broken SLA transaction, from symptom to root cause to fix.

lessons.title: Data Access and Security in Subledger Accounting

slots.practicalActivity: Review (or configure, if your environment allows) a secondary ledger with a different accounting method than your primary ledger's, confirming the same transaction can produce two different representations. Then review the data access set or security assigned to the Subledger Accounting duty role you're using.
slots.deliverable: Notes comparing a primary and secondary ledger's accounting representations for one transaction, plus the data access/security setup you reviewed.

lessons.title: Design Patterns for a Manufacturing Company

slots.practicalActivity: Modify one account rule you built earlier in this course, then rebuild accounting for a previously-accounted transaction and confirm the new rule actually changed the resulting journal. Finally, sketch your own SLA rule design (journal line rules, account rules, mapping sets) for a fictional manufacturing company's Payables accrual process, the way the lesson does for LTV Manufacturing.
slots.deliverable: One transaction with its accounting rebuilt after a rule change (showing the before/after journal difference), plus a written SLA design sketch for a manufacturing company's Payables accrual process.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After this course, a student can build and troubleshoot a complete Subledger Accounting rule chain -- journal line rules, account rules, mapping sets, and application accounting definitions -- and reconcile what it produces all the way from a subledger transaction to the General Ledger.
